cohort: The study included 114 children with anorectal malformations (ARM) treated at a single center, divided into those with and without co-occurring tethered cord syndrome (TCS).
finding: Intermediate or high-type ARM and the presence of other malformations are risk factors for the co-occurrence of tethered cord syndrome (TCS) in children with ARM, and untethering surgery significantly improved constipation in children with low-type ARM and TCS.
